title: Photon's sky, sunbeams through the clouds, and a meteor storm inside the budget
intro: What changed in method: this round copies from the packs you named (Stay True leaves and wheat, Photon's sky, Faithless items and GUI, Patrix mob skins, Soartex shelves, Conquest particles and weather) instead of inventing. It only shows answers to your round 10 feedback, so a few scenes are small and some of your picks are kept as they were. The shader scenes: Photon's sky, sunbeams through the clouds, and a meteor shower, each against round 10. Cost: High frames cost 3.3 ms at most (round 10: 3.5, budget 3.0), Low at 1080p 0.86 ms (budget 0.9), Potato at 720p 0.30 ms (budget 0.4), per frame against the same view with shaders off. High is over its budget only on the sea and swamp-water views, as in round 10; this round's three changes add at most 0.07 ms anywhere.

scenes.name: The low sun lights the whole atmosphere (Photon's sky)
scenes.question: You said the sun 'reads as a single hot spot rather than affecting the lighting of the whole atmosphere'. Cause in round 10: our sky model was physically right but only the air round the sun took its colour; the rest of the sky stayed blue-grey and our haze was a sky-coloured veil with no sunlight in it, so the land and sea never took the sunset's light. Now Photon's sky, copied: its precomputed scattering stretches the low sun's colours up the sky, its sun is tinted by the hour, and its haze is a real lit medium, thick and low at dawn and dusk, glowing toward the sun; the sea mirrors that glow. Twilight changes most: after sunset Photon keeps a lit blue hour with a pink horizon (C) where round 10 went near black (D). The trade-off: Photon's evening haze also lies over shaded ground near you, so on the golden-hour field the near grass is lifted and greyer (66,64,39 against round 10's 40,45,15); its haze density is Photon's own, not something we added. Cost: -0.12 to +0.03 ms on High across nine views (Photon's table replaces our per-frame sky march). A new sunset, B round 10, C new dusk, D round 10's dusk.
scenes.notePrompt: Does the sunset light the whole sky now? Too pink, too hazy, or right?

options.label: Photon's sky (default)
options.critic: Critic 7: Answers the note in part: the low sun now colours the whole sky, the clouds and the haze, and the sea takes the glow (upper sky 137,112,121 against round 10's 121,105,108). Against the reference it is pink-lilac, where the photo is amber-gold from the horizon up; the near islands fade into pink haze; the sun is still a thin white sliver under the cloud with no hot glow round it. Fix: a bright sun disk and aureole that blooms, with a warmer, less magenta horizon.

options.critic: Critic 8: The biggest win of the round: a lit blue hour with a pink-orange band on the horizon and readable ground, close to the reference's gradient (round 10 went near black). Two flaws: a solid white meteor streak hangs in the twilight sky in both stills and reads as a contrail, and the clouds are flat slate shapes with no pink on their undersides. Fix: no meteors until the sun is well below the horizon.

scenes.name: Sunbeams through the clouds (Photon's crepuscular rays)
scenes.question: You picked the rays 'only if we can afford them'. We can now: round 10's rays read 16 full-screen pixels per sky pixel toward the sun on screen and cost 0.31 ms at most on High (ocean sunset); Photon's, copied, march each sky pixel from your eye to the cloud base (20 steps toward the horizon, 4 overhead) through a 64x64 map of the clouds' shadow made once per frame, and cost 0.07 ms at most. They follow the real clouds, not what is on screen. Copied as is, they only added light to a sky that already holds the sunlit air's glow, so they were invisible (+1 to 3 brightness levels); now the air in a cloud's shadow also takes its share of that glow away, which is what draws the wedges. Shown on the golden-hour view, where the fan is clear (on the lake view A looked the same as off). Strength, darkest wedge over the sky round the sun (brightness levels of 255, measured on the lake): A -6, a stronger setting -10 (QF_CREP_SHADE 0.75, not shown), round 10's C -16. The open call: keep A on Medium and up as the default, ask for the stronger setting, or leave them off (B). A rays (default), B off, C round 10's rays.
scenes.notePrompt: A, stronger, or off? Is round 10's stronger fan what you liked?

options.label: Photon's rays (default)
options.critic: Critic 7: Not on the Lab, but it should be: here Photon's rays draw a clear fan of light and shadow lanes from the sun behind the hill, plainly different from rays off (p11cr0). The cost is the near field: Photon's evening haze lifts and greys the shaded grass (66,64,39 against 40,45,15).

options.label: Rays off
options.critic: Critic 6: Rays off under Photon's sky: the clouds and the warm haze are lovely, but the light has no direction near the sun; the hill and grass sit in an even pink wash with no lanes of light or shadow. Same greyed near grass as A, so that comes from the haze, not the rays.

options.label: Round 10's rays
options.critic: Critic 6: Round 10's sky with its rays: golden clouds and darker, more saturated grass (40,45,15), but the rays barely read here and the sky has the old flat band at the horizon. Shown only to compare.

scenes.name: Meteor shower from your photos, storm included, now under budget
scenes.question: From your photos: many long, thin, straight streaks, all out of one point, faint, over the Milky Way. Every meteor of a shower runs along a line through that point (the radiant), so the sky is now cut into wedges round it, each with its own meteor; a sky pixel tests only its own wedge and the two beside it: 3 meteors per pixel instead of round 10's 24 (A) or 40 (storm), so the shower's cost no longer grows with the number of meteors: the storm costs what the shower does. The radiant sits 18 to 45 degrees up; shower nights now show the Milky Way. Cost on the wide night view: A 2.99 ms, B 2.99 ms; round 10's storm 3.99 ms (budget 3.0). A shower (default), B storm (2.5x the meteors, fainter), C round 10's grazer storm.
scenes.notePrompt: Closer to your photos? Shower or storm as the default?

options.label: Shower (default), clip
options.critic: Critic 6: Closer to the photos than round 10: thin straight streaks, one or two at a time, the Milky Way present, inside the budget (2.99 ms against 3.47). Still short of the photos: the Milky Way is a dim brown dust lane, not a bright blue-white band; the star field is sparse; clouds cover half the sky; the streaks run parallel because the radiant is well out of frame, so 'all from one point' does not read. Fix: shower nights with a clear sky, a denser star field and a brighter Milky Way, and the radiant near the view.

options.label: Storm, clip
options.critic: Critic 7: The storm is nearer the owner's first photo in count, at the same cost as the shower (2.99 ms). In single frames the streaks are thin and warm; in the max-over-time sheet they are uniform white bars, all the same width and brightness, where the photo's hairlines vary a lot. The same sky problems as A (dim Milky Way, sparse stars, heavy cloud).

options.label: Round 10's storm, clip
options.critic: Critic 5: Round 10's grazer storm: level streaks with beaded trails and no radiant. Not what the photos show, and it cost 3.98 ms.

scenes.name: Stay True's leaves: the hedge
scenes.question: You asked us to stop guessing and copy Stay True. Its leaves are not frills on the edges: every leaf block carries two big round leaf clumps on vertical planes, rotated 22.5 degrees and crossing the block, so a canopy reads as soft volume instead of cubes. A is that, read straight from Stay True's model files; B is r010's edge frills; C is Stay True's textures alone.
scenes.notePrompt: Does A read like Stay True's trees? A is denser and less see-through than C (the clumps fill the gaps): is that the volume you meant, or should the leaves stay more transparent?

options.label: Stay True's leaves (r011)
options.desc: Copied from Stay True: its leaf textures, and its model: two big round leaf clumps (2 blocks wide, 1.75 tall) rotated 22.5 degrees, crossing every leaf block; each block picks one of Stay True's 2-3 variants. Measured cost, on vs off: frame time +0 to +5% (p50), leafy chunk sections carry 23% more vertices, rebuild time per section unchanged (-2%).
options.critic: Critic 7: A real copy at last: Stay True's leaves_cross model (two 2 x 1.75-block planes at 22.5 degrees, checked against its JSON). The hedge and crown get a soft, ragged volume with no spikes. The hedge still reads as a shaggy box; planes seen edge-on smear into streaks at the crown's upper left; and it is denser and less see-through than C, against the owner's 'I like the transparency'. Fix: more alpha holes in the bushy texture so light and sky show through.
